register.level: hearty, bossy, working-class (Cockney-leaning) guide: the Queen's idle retainer turned Alice's minder
register.summary: The only dream figure with consistently non-standard grammar (double negatives, 'they never executes nobody', 'she wants for to know … she do', 'this here young lady', 'He was an old crab, he was'). He is brisk and impatient — Come on!, Drive on, old fellow!, That's enough, Go on with the next verse — scornful of Alice's ignorance (simpleton, any shrimp could have told you that), and fond of explaining a pun as if it were plain fact (lessons lessen; a whiting does the boots and shoes). He deflates grandeur on principle: the Queen's executions and the Mock Turtle's sorrow are 'all fancy'. Per SUP-010 (amended BIB-0027) a photoreal CGI griffin; the eagle-shriek is spoken as a line (Hjckrrh!), not replaced by a creature sound effect.

examples.text: Why, she, It's all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know. Come on!
That's the reason they're called lessons, because they lessen from day to day.
Soles and eels, of course, any shrimp could have told you that.

sentence_style.length: short and punchy (mean 10.4, median 11 words over 43 lines); many 2-5-word shouts and orders, a few 20-35-word explanations

patterns.rule: Non-standard, working-class grammar: double negatives, subject-verb mismatch, 'for to', 'this here', tag repetition (…he was, he was / she do), 'Same as if'.

examples.text: It's all his fancy, that: he hasn't got no sorrow, you know. Come on!
This here young lady, she wants for to know your history, she do.
Hadn't time, I went to the Classics master, though. He was an old crab, he was.

patterns.rule: Brisk orders and hurry-ups to Alice and the Mock Turtle alike (Come on! / Drive on, old fellow! Don't be all day about it! / Go on with the next verse / Stand up and repeat … / Sing her … / Chorus again!).

examples.text: Drive on, old fellow! Don't be all day about it!
Stand up and repeat ''Tis the voice of the sluggard,'
Chorus again!

patterns.rule: Scorn and deflation: mocks ignorance and dismisses pretension (You ought to be ashamed … / you are a simpleton / Hold your tongue! / It's all her fancy / Hm! No accounting for tastes!).

examples.text: You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question,
Well, then, if you don't know what to uglify is, you are a simpleton.
Hm! No accounting for tastes! Sing her 'Turtle Soup,' will you, old fellow?

patterns.rule: The pun delivered as plain fact, closed with a clincher (That's the reason … / The reason is … So … So … That's all. / Now you know. / any shrimp could have told you that).

examples.text: The reason is, that they would go with the lobsters to the dance. So they got thrown out to sea. … That's all.
Boots and shoes under the sea, are done with a whiting. Now you know.
It does the boots and shoes,

patterns.rule: Impatient with explanation and sentiment: cuts subjects off and moves the entertainment on (That's enough about lessons / The adventures first, explanations take such a dreadful time / She can't explain it / I think you'd better leave off / Hadn't time).

examples.text: That's enough about lessons, tell her something about the games now.
No, no! The adventures first, explanations take such a dreadful time.
Yes, I think you'd better leave off,

patterns.rule: In the Lobster Quadrille he shouts the action beats in short exclamations over the Mock Turtle's lines (Each with a lobster as a partner! / The lobsters! / Swim after them! / Change lobsters again!).

examples.text: Each with a lobster as a partner!
Swim after them!
Change lobsters again!

preferred_fields: puns on everyday trades (lessons, whiting, soles)

examples.text: They're putting down their names, for fear they should forget them before the end of the trial.
It's all about as curious as it can be,

address.to_alice: 'you', or talks about her in the third person to the Mock Turtle ('This here young lady', 'tell her', 'Sing her'); scolding epithet 'simpleton'
address.to_mock_turtle: old fellow; refers to him as 'the Mock Turtle' when offering him to Alice
address.about_the_queen: she / her fancy — irreverent, never 'her Majesty'

examples.text: This here young lady, she wants for to know your history, she do.
Shall we try another figure of the Lobster Quadrille? Or would you like the Mock Turtle to sing you a song?

forbidden_words.reason: period drama, 1862 — his dialect is Victorian working-class, not modern slang
his register is blunt and ungrammatical; long connective reasoning is the Mouse's/Dodo's

forbidden_words.regex: \b(I beg your pardon|forgive me|I apologi[sz]e|so sorry|poor dear|how sad)\b
forbidden_words.reason: he deflates sorrow ('he hasn't got no sorrow', ch009-d0045); sighing belongs to the Mock Turtle except the one shared 'So he did' (ch009-d0082)
he calls the Queen's executions 'all her fancy' (ch009-d0042)

drift.change: Waking beside the croquet-ground: lazy, chuckling, gossiping about the Queen; then a bossy host scolding Alice at the Mock Turtle's ledge.
Lobster Quadrille: manic, shouting the dance beats with bounds into the air; then a know-all explainer of puns; ends hurrying Alice off (Come on!).
In court: drops to a whisper, a knowing aside to Alice about the jury.
